entities.name: Scabies
entities.description: Contagious ectoparasitic skin infestation caused by Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis, clinically characterized by intense nocturnal pruritus, pathognomonic serpiginous intraepidermal burrows, male genital nodules, and secondary pyoderma.

entities.name: Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis
entities.description: Obligate human microscopic ectoparasitic mite (Arachnida, Acari; adult females 0.3–0.45 mm) that excavates the epidermal stratum corneum, depositing 2–3 eggs daily and dark brown fecal pellets (scybala).

entities.name: Direct Prolonged Skin-to-Skin Contact
entities.description: Continuous close skin contact for at least 10 to 20 minutes (holding hands, co-sleeping, sexual intimacy) required for transfer of low mite burdens in classical scabies.

entities.name: Overcrowded Institutional or Enclosed Community Settings
entities.description: High-density residential environments including refugee camps, prisons, day-care centers, residential aged-care facilities, and remote tropical island communities where crowding accelerates mite transmission.

entities.name: Severe Immunocompromise or Cognitive and Physical Debility
entities.description: Defective cell-mediated immunity (advanced HIV/AIDS, HTLV-1 coinfection, solid-organ transplantation, immunosuppressive therapy) or physical/cognitive debility preventing scratching, predisposing to hyperinfestation crusted scabies.

entities.name: Fomite Contamination via Shed Scales and Bedding in Crusted Scabies
entities.description: Indirect transmission route through shed hyperkeratotic crusts, unwashed clothing, and contaminated bed linen harboring millions of viable mites shedding from patients with crusted scabies.

entities.name: Serpiginous Burrows in Interdigital Web Spaces and Wrists
entities.description: Delicate, thread-like, slightly elevated, wavy or sinuous grayish-white or light brownish intraepidermal tunnels (1–10 mm long) terminating in a pinpoint papule or vesicle, pathognomonic for scabies (2020 IACS Level B1).

entities.name: Exquisitely Pruritic Inflammatory Nodules on Penile Shaft and Scrotum
entities.description: Firm, indurated, exquisitely pruritic erythematous or violaceous inflammatory nodules on the penis and scrotum in males representing delayed hypersensitivity, highly specific for scabies (2020 IACS Level B2).

entities.name: Intense Nocturnal Pruritus Sparing Head and Neck in Adults
entities.description: Severe, unrelenting pruritus characteristically worsening dramatically at night and after warm baths, developing 3–6 weeks post-primary infection, with strict sparing of the adult head, scalp, face, and neck.

entities.name: Hyperkeratotic Crusted Norwegian Scabies in Immunocompromised Hosts
entities.description: Massive, adherent, fissured yellow-gray or brown hyperkeratotic crusts involving the hands, feet, scalp, and subungual spaces (onychauxis) harboring millions of mites, often with mild or absent pruritus.

entities.name: Diffuse Polymorphic Acropustulosis Involving Palms Soles and Scalp in Infants
entities.description: Atypical distribution in infants under 2 years where the adult sparing rule breaks down, presenting as widespread inflammatory papules, vesicles, pustules, and burrows on the scalp, face, retroauricular folds, palms, and soles.

entities.name: Delta-Wing Jet Sign on High-Resolution Dermoscopy
entities.description: Bedside dermoscopic hallmark (10–20x magnification) revealing a dark, triangular or delta-shaped structure (mite head and forelegs) at the leading terminus of a sinuous translucent intraepidermal track ('jet with vapor contrail', 2020 IACS Level A3).

entities.name: Microscopic Identification of Mites Ova or Scybala from Skin Scrapings
entities.description: Direct optical light microscopy (10–40x) of mineral oil skin scrapings definitively identifying adult female mites (0.3–0.4 mm with 4 pairs of legs), translucent oval eggs (100–150 µm), or dark brown fecal pellets (scybala) (2020 IACS Level A1).

entities.name: Marked Hyper-IgE and Severe Peripheral Eosinophilia in Crusted Scabies
entities.description: Laboratory hallmark in crusted scabies showing severe peripheral blood eosinophilia (>30–50%) and marked serum IgE elevation (>1,000–10,000 IU/mL), contrasted with normal or mild eosinophilia (5–15%) in classical scabies.

entities.name: Positive Burrow Ink Test on Superficial Epidermis
entities.description: Bedside diagnostic maneuver where surgical pen ink rubbed across a suspected lesion and wiped with alcohol highlights a distinct zig-zag or wavy intraepidermal track by capillary filling of the burrow.

entities.name: Complete Absence of Pruritus in an Immunocompetent Host
entities.description: Total lack of pruritus in an immunocompetent adult or child virtually excludes classical scabies, as delayed-type cell-mediated hypersensitivity to mite antigens universally causes severe itch.

entities.name: Pruritic Eruption Involving Face Scalp and Neck in an Immunocompetent Adult
entities.description: Pruritic rash involving the face, scalp, and neck in an adult immunocompetent host violates the anatomical 'rule of sparing' and strongly excludes classical scabies, indicating alternative dermatoses.

entities.name: Non-Pruritic Palmoplantar Maculopapular Rash with Generalized Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Palmoplantar maculopapular eruption that lacks pruritus and presents with generalized nontender lymphadenopathy or condyloma lata excludes scabies, confirming secondary syphilis.

entities.name: Silvery Extensor Scaly Plaques with Auspitz Sign and Negative Skin Scraping
entities.description: Thick silvery plaques on extensor surfaces (elbows, knees) displaying punctate bleeding upon scale removal (Auspitz sign) with zero mites or eggs on mineral oil scraping excludes crusted scabies and confirms plaque psoriasis.

entities.name: Atopic Dermatitis
entities.description: Chronic inflammatory pruriginous dermatosis primarily affecting flexural folds (antecubital and popliteal fossae), neck, and face, lacking intraepidermal burrows and penile nodules.

entities.name: Papular Urticaria and Arthropod Bites
entities.description: Hypersensitivity reaction to insect bites characterized by clustered wheals and papules on exposed limbs without web-space predilection, burrows, or genital nodules.

entities.name: Plaque Psoriasis
entities.description: Immune-mediated dermatosis producing silvery micaceous plaques on extensor surfaces, mimicking crusted scabies but lacking mites and exhibiting the Auspitz sign.

entities.name: Secondary Syphilis
entities.description: Systemic Treponema pallidum infection causing ham-colored maculopapular eruptions on palms and soles, constitutional symptoms, generalized lymphadenopathy, and positive treponemal serologies.

entities.name: Topical 5% Permethrin Cream with Mandatory Day 7-14 Reapplication
entities.description: First-line neurotoxic scabicide applied neck-to-toes for 8–14 hours; requires a mandatory second application 7 to 14 days later to eradicate newly hatched nymphs because it lacks complete ovicidal efficacy.

entities.name: Oral Ivermectin with Mandatory Day 7-14 Repeat Dosing
entities.description: First-line systemic scabicide (200 µg/kg single oral dose); requires a mandatory second dose 7 to 14 days later due to lack of ovicidal activity, ideal for institutional outbreaks and mass drug administration.

entities.name: Simultaneous Treatment of All Household and Sexual Contacts
entities.description: Epidemiological requirement to treat all co-habiting household members and close physical contacts concurrently regardless of symptoms, preventing reinfection from asymptomatic incubation-phase carriers.

entities.name: Intensive Combination Therapy with Topical Permethrin Oral Ivermectin and Keratolytics
entities.description: Mandatory multimodal regimen for crusted scabies comprising repeated oral Ivermectin (multiple doses across 4 weeks), daily topical 5% Permethrin, and topical keratolytics (5% salicylic acid or 40% urea) to debride thick crusts.

entities.name: Persistence of Post-Scabietic Pruritus Despite Parasitological Cure
entities.description: Benign continuation of pruritus for 2 to 4 weeks post-treatment caused by lingering dead mite antigens in the stratum corneum; responds to emollients and mild topical steroids rather than repeated scabicides.

entities.name: Single-Dose Scabicidal Monotherapy
entities.description: Monotherapy with a single application of permethrin or single dose of oral ivermectin without day 7-14 re-treatment; leads to clinical relapse because neither agent is reliably ovicidal.

relationships.target: Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Scabies is caused by Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis, an obligate human microscopic ectoparasitic mite (0.3-0.45 mm) that excavates intraepidermal burrows within the stratum corneum, depositing eggs and fecal pellets (scybala).

relationships.target: Direct Prolonged Skin-to-Skin Contact
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Transmission of classical scabies occurs predominantly through direct, prolonged skin-to-skin contact (typically requiring at least 10–20 minutes of continuous physical contact, such as holding hands, co-sleeping, or sexual contact) due to a low average mite burden (10-15 mites).

relationships.target: Overcrowded Institutional or Enclosed Community Settings
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] High-risk environments include overcrowded tropical communities, refugee and displaced person camps, prisons, day-care centers, boarding schools, and long-term residential aged-care facilities where close contact facilitates mite spread.

relationships.target: Severe Immunocompromise or Cognitive and Physical Debility
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, host susceptibility, defective cell-mediated immunity
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Defective cell-mediated immunity (advanced HIV/AIDS, HTLV-1 coinfection, solid-organ transplantation, prolonged corticosteroid therapy) or physical/cognitive debility preventing normal scratching responses predisposes to hyperinfestation crusted (Norwegian) scabies.

relationships.target: Fomite Contamination via Shed Scales and Bedding in Crusted Scabies
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] While fomite transmission is rare and inefficient in classical scabies, indirect transmission readily occurs from patients with crusted scabies via shedding of millions of viable mites in exfoliated keratin crusts, clothing, towels, bedding, and room dust.

relationships.target: Serpiginous Burrows in Interdigital Web Spaces and Wrists
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Delicate, thread-like, slightly elevated, wavy or serpiginous grayish-white or brownish intraepidermal tunnels (1–10 mm in length) terminating in a tiny papule or vesicle harboring the female mite, characteristically found on finger web spaces, volar wrists, and ankles (2020 IACS Level B1).

relationships.target: Exquisitely Pruritic Inflammatory Nodules on Penile Shaft and Scrotum
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, pathognomonic male genital sign, nodular scabies
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Exquisitely itchy, firm, indurated erythematous or violaceous inflammatory papules and nodules on the penile shaft, glans, prepuce, and scrotum represent a pathognomonic delayed hypersensitivity hallmark in males (2020 IACS Level B2) that may persist for months.

relationships.target: Intense Nocturnal Pruritus Sparing Head and Neck in Adults
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, cardinal clinical sign, nocturnal itch
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Severe, unrelenting pruritus characteristically worsening at night and after warm baths, developing 3–6 weeks after initial infestation or within 24–48 hours upon reinfection, with classic sparing of the head, scalp, face, and neck in adult patients.

relationships.target: Hyperkeratotic Crusted Norwegian Scabies in Immunocompromised Hosts
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Massive, thick, adherent, fissured yellow-gray or brown hyperkeratotic scales and crusts affecting hands, feet, scalp, and subungual nail beds (onychauxis) harboring millions of viable mites; itch is characteristically diminished or absent.

relationships.target: Diffuse Polymorphic Acropustulosis Involving Palms Soles and Scalp in Infants
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] In infants and children under 2 years of age, the classic adult distribution breaks down, presenting as diffuse inflammatory papules, vesicles, pustules, and burrows involving the scalp, face, retroauricular folds, palms, and soles (infantile acropustulosis pattern).

relationships.target: Delta-Wing Jet Sign on High-Resolution Dermoscopy
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Bedside dermoscopy at 10–20x magnification visualizes a dark, pigmented triangular structure (mite head and forelegs) at the distal end of a sinuous translucent intraepidermal track ('delta-wing jet with contrail sign'), definitively confirming active scabies (2020 IACS Level A3).

relationships.target: Microscopic Identification of Mites Ova or Scybala from Skin Scrapings
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, definitive microscopic confirmation, skin scraping
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Light microscopy (10–40x) of mineral oil skin scrapings taken from an unexcoriated burrow definitively demonstrates the adult female mite (0.3–0.45 mm with 4 pairs of legs), translucent oval eggs (100–150 µm), or dark brown fecal pellets (scybala) (2020 IACS Level A1).

relationships.target: Marked Hyper-IgE and Severe Peripheral Eosinophilia in Crusted Scabies
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, laboratory hallmark, crusted scabies lab
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] While routine CBC in classical scabies is normal or shows mild eosinophilia (5-15%), crusted scabies characteristically produces profound peripheral eosinophilia (>30-50%) and massive serum IgE elevations (>1,000–10,000 IU/mL) reflecting unchecked Th2 immune polarization.

relationships.target: Positive Burrow Ink Test on Superficial Epidermis
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, bedside diagnostic test, ink tracking
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Bedside application of surgical pen or fountain pen ink followed by alcohol wipe removal demonstrates distinctive linear, zig-zag ink tracking into the open stratum corneum burrow tunnel, confirming burrow architecture at triage.

relationships.target: Complete Absence of Pruritus in an Immunocompetent Host
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Complete absence of pruritus in an immunocompetent adult or child virtually rules out classical scabies, as the cell-mediated delayed hypersensitivity reaction to mite antigens invariably generates intense itch.

relationships.target: Pruritic Eruption Involving Face Scalp and Neck in an Immunocompetent Adult
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, anatomical sparing rule
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] A pruritic papular eruption involving the face, scalp, and neck in an immunocompetent adult violates the cardinal 'rule of sparing' and strongly excludes classical scabies, indicating instead atopic or seborrheic dermatitis.

relationships.target: Non-Pruritic Palmoplantar Maculopapular Rash with Generalized Lymphadenopathy
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] A palmoplantar maculopapular rash that is non-pruritic and accompanied by generalized lymphadenopathy, mucous patches, or positive treponemal serology excludes scabies in favor of secondary syphilis.

relationships.target: Silvery Extensor Scaly Plaques with Auspitz Sign and Negative Skin Scraping
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Thick, silvery, micaceous scaly plaques on extensor surfaces (elbows, knees) exhibiting punctate bleeding upon scale removal (Auspitz sign) and completely negative skin scrapings for mites excludes crusted scabies and confirms plaque psoriasis.

relationships.target: Atopic Dermatitis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Atopic dermatitis predominantly affects the flexural antecubital and popliteal folds, neck, and face, features personal or family atopic diathesis, lacks discrete linear burrows and penile nodules, lacks the dermoscopic delta-wing sign, and does not simultaneously affect asymptomatic household contacts.

relationships.target: Papular Urticaria and Arthropod Bites
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Papular urticaria presents with episodic, clustered wheals and excoriated erythematous papules on exposed extremities (classic 'breakfast, lunch, and dinner' distribution) without intraepidermal burrows, web space involvement, or genital nodules.

relationships.target: Plaque Psoriasis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Plaque psoriasis (the chief mimic of crusted scabies) presents with well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scales on extensor surfaces with positive Auspitz sign and zero mites, whereas crusted scabies features diffuse yellow-gray fissured crusts teeming with thousands of live mites, eggs, and scybala on mineral oil scraping.

relationships.target: Secondary Syphilis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Secondary syphilis features non-pruritic, coppery, ham-colored macules and papules on the palms and soles, constitutional symptoms, generalized non-tender lymphadenopathy, and reactive RPR/VDRL serology, whereas scabies is intensely pruritic (worse nocturnally), demonstrates burrows, and spares the adult head/face.

relationships.target: Topical 5% Permethrin Cream with Mandatory Day 7-14 Reapplication
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, first-line topical scabicide, therapeutic cure
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Classical scabies responds to overnight application (8–14 hours) of topical 5% Permethrin cream applied from neck to soles; a mandatory second application 7 to 14 days later is required to eradicate newly hatched nymphs before sexual maturity due to incomplete ovicidal action.

relationships.target: Oral Ivermectin with Mandatory Day 7-14 Repeat Dosing
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, first-line oral scabicide, systemic therapy
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Scabies responds to oral Ivermectin (200 µg/kg single dose with food/water); a mandatory second dose 7 to 14 days later is strictly required because ivermectin lacks activity against scabies eggs.

relationships.target: Simultaneous Treatment of All Household and Sexual Contacts
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Verification of definitive cure requires simultaneous treatment of all cohabiting household members and close contacts regardless of symptoms to eliminate incubation-phase mites (3-6 week delay) and avoid ping-pong re-infestation.

relationships.target: Intensive Combination Therapy with Topical Permethrin Oral Ivermectin and Keratolytics
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, intensive combination protocol, crusted scabies
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Crusted (Norwegian) scabies is refractory to monotherapy and responds to combination therapy: daily topical 5% Permethrin cream for 1-2 weeks plus multiple oral Ivermectin doses (days 1, 2, 8, 9, 15, and up to 22/29) combined with topical keratolytics (5% salicylic acid or 40% urea) to break down thick protective scales.

relationships.target: Persistence of Post-Scabietic Pruritus Despite Parasitological Cure
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, post-treatment allergic pruritus, clinical verification
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Pruritus characteristically persists for 2 to 4 weeks after successful mite eradication due to retained dead parasite antigens (post-scabietic itch); this delayed resolution does not represent treatment failure and responds to emollients and mild topical steroids rather than repeated scabicides.

relationships.target: Single-Dose Scabicidal Monotherapy
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Scabies eggs are intrinsically resistant to single-dose neurotoxic scabicide monotherapy (both permethrin and ivermectin lack reliable ovicidal activity); failure to repeat dosing at 7–14 days allows surviving eggs to hatch into viable nymphs, causing clinical relapse.
